title: An AI data centre in Seine-Saint-Denis
titleFr: Un centre de données IA en Seine-Saint-Denis
summary: A hypothetical 200 MW AI computing campus in La Courneuve (Seine-Saint-Denis): who is affected, who would object and why, and whose voices a public meeting would miss.
proposalFr: PROJET HYPOTHÉTIQUE — avis de concertation préalable (exercice de simulation). Un opérateur propose de construire un campus de calcul pour l'intelligence artificielle dans la zone industrielle Rateau, à La Courneuve. Le site d'environ 8 hectares, aujourd'hui occupé par des entrepôts et ateliers, accueillerait trois bâtiments de 28 m de haut au maximum, pour une puissance électrique de 200 mégawatts. Le chantier durerait environ quatre ans, en trois phases, avec un poste électrique sur le site et deux lignes souterraines de 225 000 volts creusées sous la voirie jusqu'aux postes voisins. Le refroidissement fonctionnerait en circuit fermé (environ 5 000 m³ d'eau par an). Une centaine de groupes électrogènes de secours seraient testés chaque mois. L'opérateur s'engagerait à livrer jusqu'à 15 MW de chaleur au réseau de chauffage urbain, soit l'équivalent d'environ 5 000 logements. Il annonce environ 600 emplois au pic du chantier et 120 emplois permanents sur le site. Les recettes fiscales locales sont estimées entre 6 et 9 millions d'euros par an. Votre avis est sollicité. (Une position favorable (+) signifie soutenir le projet.)
proposalEn: HYPOTHETICAL PROJECT — notice of prior public consultation (simulation exercise). An operator proposes to build an artificial-intelligence computing campus in the Rateau industrial zone in La Courneuve. The site of about 8 hectares, now used by warehouses and workshops, would host three buildings up to 28 m high, drawing 200 megawatts of electricity. Construction would take about four years in three phases, with an on-site substation and two underground 225,000-volt lines dug under the streets to nearby substations. Cooling would run in a closed loop (about 5,000 m³ of water a year). Around a hundred backup generators would be tested every month. The operator would commit to supply up to 15 MW of heat to the district-heating network, roughly the needs of 5,000 homes. It announces about 600 jobs at the peak of construction and 120 permanent jobs on site. Local tax revenue is estimated at 6 to 9 million euros a year. Your opinion is invited.

uncertainty.method: K=3 proposal paraphrases × 2 models (NVIDIA-Nemotron-3-Nano-30B-A3B, nemotron-3-super-120b-a12b) on a random 300-resident subsample; yesRange = full-sample yes share shifted by the min/max deviation of the runs from the main run on that subsample (MOCK: seeded noise, not real model variation)

notes: MOCK RUN: no language model was called (no API key). Stances and texts come from simple deterministic heuristics and templates marked [demo]/[démo].
Every text is a simulated voice generated for a synthetic resident, never a real person. Results are hypotheses to test, not evidence of public opinion.

Participation: logit(p) = logit(participationBase or participationPropensity) + 0.35·exposure + 0.5·(LLM self-report − 0.5) + c, with c = -2.552 calibrated so expected participants = 3.00% of the 2000 residents in scope. The LLM self-report is only a weak rank modifier. For this public meeting, attendance also decays with distance from the site (-0.25 log-odds per km beyond 2 km, capped at -2.5). The highlighted attendees on the map are one seeded random draw; all attendee numbers use the probability weights.

Neighbour talk: 280 random pairs (208 within 300 m, the rest in the same district); 49 of 560 residents changed stance. Arguments that travelled most: Electricity and water use (120); Europe needs its own AI infrastructure (75); Too far away to matter to me (68).
Hypothetical project: site and parameters come from pipeline/data/ground_truth/datacenter_context.json (invented but plausible, modelled on real Seine-Saint-Denis campuses); it is not a real project.

Turnout assumption: about 3% of all residents of the study area engage with the consultation (meeting, online contribution or register). This is an upper-range planning figure chosen so the 'attendees' view is readable; real public debates often reach well under 1%. Who engages matters more than how many.
Imputed attributes (car, heavy car, tenure, nationality, workplace) come from INSEE statistics, not from the NVIDIA dataset, and are labelled as imputed.
